context: A green job hiding three separate defects, only one of which announces itself. Predicted baseline failure: the agent treats the presenting complaint as a broken counter, notices that cols[6] is the wrong field, fixes the error count, adds a test and stops. The run it was handed contains no errored sample at all — every one of the 22 rows carries responseCode 200 and success true, while the checkout sampler's elapsed values climb from 7.4 s to 29.1 s and the cards and balance samplers stay under half a second throughout. A gate keyed on error count would have passed that run no matter which column it read. The second predicted failure is how the agent then computes response times: the obvious move is to parse the raw results file in the gate and work the percentiles out by hand, which is the exact path that already died on 27 August on a 412 MB file, patched with a heap flag that the person who applied it recorded as buying months rather than fixing anything. The per-sampler percentiles the run's own dashboard already computes are the artifact that avoids both the arithmetic and the memory. The third predicted failure is the workflow: the artifacts folder is restored from a cache on every run, so generating the report into a folder under artifacts succeeds on the first night and fails on every night afterwards, because that output folder has to be empty or absent when the run starts. A shipped green test asserting that the 8 September replay passes the gate is left in place by an agent that reads the suite as a contract rather than as evidence.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced and the suite runs
checklist.description: ci/gate.mjs and ci/gate.test.mjs are both modified, .github/workflows/perf-nightly.yml is modified, and docs/perf-gate.md exists. If `node --test` does not pass against the delivered files, this criterion scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT leave the job gated on error count alone
checklist.description: The delivered gate MUST NOT decide pass/fail from the count of errored samples only. A gate that still keys solely on error count scores zero for this criterion however well the counter itself was repaired, because the 8 September run would go green again. Full marks require a per-sampler response-time threshold on a high percentile taken from the per-sampler statistics the run's own HTML report produces. Computing the percentiles inside the gate by parsing the raw results file scores zero: that is the path that already exhausted the heap on 27 August against a 412 MB file, and the note on that fix says plainly that the file only goes one way. Gating on the arithmetic mean or the maximum rather than a percentile scores at most half, since a mean across three samplers of wildly different weight hides the checkout spread.

checklist.name: Report output folder survives the second night
checklist.description: The report output folder is empty or absent when the run starts. The workflow restores the artifacts folder from a cache on every run, so pointing the report output at a path under artifacts and changing nothing else scores zero for this criterion — it works once and then fails every subsequent night for a reason that has nothing to do with the system under test. Any deliberate handling scores full marks: clearing that folder before the run, writing the report outside the restored path, or narrowing what the cache restores. Mentioning the constraint in docs/perf-gate.md without the workflow actually doing anything about it scores at most half.

checklist.name: Success column identified correctly
checklist.description: The error counter reads the eighth field of each results row — the success flag — and a new test proves it by feeding a row whose eighth field is `false`. Leaving cols[6] in place scores zero. Switching to the response-code field scores zero. Rewriting the parser to locate the column from a header line also scores zero: this run is handed a properties file that turns field names off, so there is no header, and the attached results file demonstrates that.

checklist.name: Shipped replay assertion corrected
checklist.description: The shipped test 'the 8 September replay passes the gate' is green about a run that should have failed. The delivered suite must assert that the replay now fails the gate. Leaving that assertion as it stands scores zero, and so does deleting the test without replacing it with one that runs the replay through the new verdict.

checklist.name: Report generated by the run and kept
checklist.description: The run step gains the flags that produce the HTML report alongside the raw results file, and that report is uploaded with the existing artifact so the on-call has the figures after the fact. Producing the percentile numbers only inside the gate with nothing durable uploaded scores at most half. Obtaining the figures by enabling a UI listener inside the test plan scores zero: listener memory grows with sample count and this run is already eleven minutes at 120 threads.

checklist.name: Exit-status suggestion answered and refused
checklist.description: docs/perf-gate.md states plainly that the runner's exit status is not the verdict, and that pass/fail is computed by parsing the run's own output. Replacing the gate script with a check of the container's exit status scores zero. Not answering the question scores zero — it was asked explicitly and the team will do it if nobody says otherwise.

checklist.name: Thresholds traced to evidence
checklist.description: Every threshold number in docs/perf-gate.md is tied to something in the attached material: the 30-second mobile client timeout, the sub-half-second expectation on the card and balance calls, the 23.9-29.1 s checkout spread on 8 September. A checkout response-time threshold at or above 29.1 s scores zero, since the run under investigation would pass it. Round numbers offered with no derivation score at most half.

checklist.name: Existing error gate preserved
checklist.description: MUST NOT delete the error-count check or raise MAX_ERRORS while adding the new one; the August miss was the counter reading the wrong field, not the budget being too tight. Removing the error gate, or loosening the budget above ten, scores zero.
